beginner.stem: How many protons does a Rhodium atom have? (That number is also its place on the table.)
beginner.explanation: Rhodium is element 45. A neutral atom has 45 protons and 45 electrons.

beginner.stem: Which element has the symbol Rh?

beginner.stem: Compare catalog boiling point: Rhodium vs Molybdenum. Which is larger?

beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Rhodium?
beginner.explanation: Rhodium in a car's converter helps turn nitrogen oxides in the exhaust into nitrogen gas. A thin coat does the work.

beginner.stem: Which of these is a listed use of Rhodium?
beginner.explanation: Rhodium plating is a hard, silvery finish on some jewelry and on optical mirrors. It does not tarnish.

beginner.explanation: Rhodium is one of the rarest and most expensive metals in use. The converter holds milligrams, not a bar.

beginner.stem: In which year does this catalog place the discovery of Rhodium?
beginner.explanation: Rhodium is listed as discovered in 1803.

beginner.stem: Who does this catalog credit for finding Rhodium?
beginner.explanation: The catalog credits William Hyde Wollaston for Rhodium.

beginner.stem: Which history line belongs to Rhodium?
options: Stanley Thompson, Albert Ghiorso, and Glenn Seaborg produced element 97 at Berkeley in 1949 by bombarding americium with alpha particles.
Seaborg, James, and Ghiorso produced element 96 in 1944 by bombarding plutonium with alpha particles.
William Hyde Wollaston, working in secret on platinum residues, isolated rhodium in 1803.

beginner.stem: How does the catalog describe the discovery of Rhodium?
options: William Hyde Wollaston dissolved crude platinum in aqua regia, precipitated the platinum as the ammonium salt, and was left with a rose-red solution.
Molybdenite looks like graphite and was used as a pencil ore.
Stanley Thompson, Albert Ghiorso, and Glenn Seaborg bombarded a target of americium-241 with helium ions in 1949.
Seaborg, James, and Ghiorso bombarded plutonium-239 with helium ions in the Berkeley cyclotron in 1944.
beginner.explanation: William Hyde Wollaston dissolved crude platinum in aqua regia, precipitated the platinum as the ammonium salt, and was left with a rose-red solution.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Rhodium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: William Hyde Wollaston worked privately on platinum residues and in 1803 isolated a metal he announced together with palladium.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Rhodium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: The new metal’s chloride solutions were rose red, and Wollaston took the name rhodium from the Greek word for that flower.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Rhodium in this catalog?
options: A Price That Will Not Sit
beginner.explanation: Rhodium stayed the scarcest and costliest of the classic platinum metals, and its price has leapt and crashed with the car industry.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Rhodium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: A very thin coat of rhodium turns jewelry and optical parts into a hard, bright surface that resists tarnish far better than the metal underneath.

beginner.stem: Which story title belongs to Rhodium in this catalog?
beginner.explanation: When governments demanded cleaner exhaust, rhodium took a narrow catalytic job that platinum by itself did not cover as well.

beginner.stem: One listed emission line of Rhodium is near which wavelength?
beginner.explanation: The catalog lists a Rhodium line at 343.49 nm (UV).
